Yuri Gagarin, at 27, made history as the first human to journey into space, orbiting the Earth on 12 April 1961, in Vostok 1, launched from Baikonur Cosmodrome. His flight lasted 108 minutes, breaking the bounds of Earth's gravity. Born to a carpenter father and a mother who worked as a milkmaid, Gagarin's early life was marked by displacement during World War II. Upon his return, Gagarin achieved global fame, touring countries like Germany, Canada and Japan to showcase Soviet technological prowess.
